info.title: ERP API
info.description:
Every response carries the same envelope: `{ "success": true, "data": … }` on success, `{ "success": false, "error": { "code", "message" } }` on failure. List endpoints add a `pagination` object alongside `data`.

**Money** is serialised as a *string* (`"1080.00"`), never a JSON number — numbers are IEEE-754 doubles and would quietly lose cents. Send it back the same way. Totals are always computed server-side.

**Sorting** uses `?sort=column` or `?sort=-column` for descending. Each endpoint has its own allow-list; anything outside it falls back to that endpoint's default rather than erroring, since a column name cannot be a bound parameter.

cancelled nor adjusted. This does not touch the status machine — it
recomputes settlement, and what is now owed back shows as a negative
`amount_due`.

The honest caveat, carried to the screen rather than buried in a comment.

posted at all, and the credit for that part has nothing behind it.

The browser loads this URL straight from the object store, which keeps receipt traffic out of the API — and, more practically, means an `` works: the session here is a bearer token in a header, and an image tag cannot send one.

tax_rate.description: A whole percentage: 20 means 20%, the same convention as everywhere else.

CreatePurchaseReturnRequest.description:

warehouse — stock has to leave from somewhere in particular.

reason.description: Why the goods went back, in whatever words fit.

rate.description: A whole percentage: 20 means 20%, matching `tax_rate` on document lines.

CreditNote.description:
Crediting a customer: the counterpart of an [`Invoice`].

Stores its own totals, unlike a purchase return which derives them from the
order. The reason is not convention: `invoice_entries` derives its revenue leg
as `base_total − base_tax` so that rounding cannot leave the legs disagreeing
with the receivable, and a credit note has to reverse that identically —
which needs a stored total to be the remainder's anchor.

fx_rate.description:
The *invoice's* rate. The receivable was raised at it, so relieving it at
any other would leave a difference nothing accounts for.

reason.description: Why it was issued, in whatever words fit.

warehouse_id.description:
Where returned goods landed. `None` is ordinary and means the credit is
money only — a price dispute or an over-billing.

invoice_line_id.description:
Everything about the price comes from here — a credit is worth what was
charged, not what the item is worth today.

DeletedResponse.description: Response for DELETE handlers, which have no body to return.

DocumentLineRequest.description:
One line on a quote, order or invoice. The three documents share a line
shape, so they share a request type.

`Serialize` is required by `validator`, which echoes the offending value back
in the error payload when a `length` rule fails on the containing `Vec`.

tax_rate.description:
A whole percentage: 20 means 20%, the same convention as
`accounting.tax_rates.rate`.

annual_leave_entitlement.description: Paid leave days granted per calendar year.

base_salary.description:
`salary` restated in the base currency — payroll cost is only additive
across a workforce paid in different currencies once restated.

code.description: Repeats the HTTP status, so a client that only kept the body still knows.

message.description:
Human-readable. Validation failures list every offending field as

Every entry is one balanced pair: `amount` is debited from one account and
credited to another, so the ledger can never go out of balance by construction.

base_amount.description:

order_status.description: Status the parent order ended up in after this receipt.

InventoryOpeningReport.description:
What switching to perpetual costing would put on the balance sheet.

A preview rather than an action, because the figure deserves a look before it
is posted: see the caveat on `assumes_everything_was_received`.

already_posted.description: True once the opening entry exists. Posting again writes nothing.

assumes_everything_was_received.description:
The honest caveat, carried to the screen rather than buried in a comment.

The entry credits Cost of sales because goods received under periodic
costing were expensed there on arrival, so this reverses an
over-expensing. Stock that arrived through a hand-made movement was never
posted at all, and the credit for that part has nothing behind it.

perpetual_inventory.description:
False while the inventory accounts are unmapped, in which case there is
nothing to open and posting would have nowhere to go.

base_amount_paid.description:

These answer "what is still outstanding on this invoice", which is a
question about the invoice. What the money was actually worth when it
arrived lives on the payment, along with the difference between the two.

order_line_id.description:
The order line this is billing, when the invoice came from an order.

What an order line has left to bill is summed from these, so the link is
the whole mechanism behind partial fulfilment. `None` for an invoice
raised straight against a customer.

signed_out.description:
Always true — the endpoint errors rather than reporting a sign-out that
did not take effect.

base_value.description:
`value` restated in the base currency. Pipeline by stage sums this, so
that deals in different currencies can be added at all.

OrderLineView.description:
An order line with how much of it is still to be billed.

The mirror of `PurchaseOrderLineView`, except that `invoiced` is derived from
the order's live invoices rather than read off the row, so the view is built
with it rather than `From` the line alone.

OrganizationSettings.description:

quote or an invoice.

Exactly one row exists. See `011_organization_settings.sql` for why this is

ar_account_id.description:

All five together are what switches automatic posting on: an

default_dispatch_warehouse_id.description:

application behaved before automatic dispatch existed. Setting it also
turns on a refusal: an invoice the shelf cannot cover stops being
issuable. See `022_default_dispatch_warehouse.sql`.

base_opening_balance.description:
The balances restated in the base currency, so that a trial balance over

items.description:

which needs a stored total to be the remainder's anchor.

reason.description: Why it was issued, in whatever words fit.

tags.description: Products, warehouses, stock levels and bills of materials. Levels only ever change through a movement.

tags.description: Vendors, purchase orders and goods receipts. Receiving posts stock and advances the order in one transaction.

tags.description: Chart of accounts, double-entry ledger, tax rates and reports. Restricted to accountants and managers.

tags.name: Files
